title: Reliability Ops Docking Plan and Quiet Launch Protocol — SLO Adoption Pilot
content:
Purpose:
This doc outlines a cross-functional 'docking' plan to onboard 3 pilot product teams to production SLOs with a quiet (low-customer-impact) launch. The aim is to validate telemetry, escalation paths, and runbook handoffs before a wider SLO rollout. The approach minimizes customer exposure and gives the SRE and platform teams a controlled environment to iterate.

Scope:
- Pilot scope: Feature-level serving endpoints for two customer-facing routes + internal admin API.
- Participants: SRE, Platform, Serving Runtime, Product (two teams), Observability, Customer Success (on-call shadow).
- Timebox: 8 weeks from kickoff to review (with a 4-week active observation window).

Core principles:
1) Docking first, enforce later — focus on safe attachment of teams to observability and escalation furniture rather than rigid early enforcement of penalties.
2) Quiet launch — route small percentage of traffic via shadowing and canary headers to surface real-world signals without impacting most customers.
3) Iterative telemetry tuning — start with broad signals then refine SLO measurement windows and noise filters.
4) Human-in-the-loop escalation — prefer manual acknowledge-and-tune cycles during the pilot.

Milestones and timeline (high-level):
- Week 0: Kickoff + stakeholder alignment (roles, goals, success criteria).
- Week 1: Telemetry plumbing and test traffic (observability validates spans, traces, token-level latency histograms).
- Week 2: Define SLOs and SLI calculation notebook + runbook skeleton.
- Week 3: Quiet-path canary (0.5%–2% traffic) and traffic shadowing to produce realistic KV cache behavior.
- Week 4–7: Observation window (collect signals, run tabletop exercises, iterate thresholds).
- Week 8: Post-mortem & go/no-go recommendations for full enforcement or expanded pilot.

Success criteria (pilot exit):
- SLIs are stable: measurement variance < 6% over 7 days after filters applied.
- Runbooks executed successfully in at least one injection test and one real minor incident handled within target MTTR.
- Teams have completed SLO onboarding checklist and dry-run of pager handoff.
- No customer-facing SLA breach outside the quiet-path traffic fraction.

Roles and responsibilities (docking matrix):
- SRE (lead): overall reliability plan, escalation matrix, incident facilitator for pilot tests.
- Observability team: implement measurement queries, dashboard templates, alert tuning.
- Serving Runtime: provide kernel-level telemetry hooks and guidance for batching/kv-cache metrics.
- Product teams: finalize target endpoints, accept canary headers, participate in tabletop runbooks.
- Platform (RBAC/network): configure access, create quiet-path routing policy, ensure VPC rules for private pilots.
- Customer Success (shadow): validate customer impact signals and prepare messaging templates.

Quiet-launch technical pattern (implementation checklist):
1) Feature flag gate + canary header: add header to route small percentage of production traffic.
2) Shadow copy: replicate a configurable subset of requests to pilot cluster for telemetry capture (no effect on responses).
3) Metric tagging: include team_id, route_version, batch_size, kv_cache_hit for SLI slicing.
4) Aggregation: use 1m and 5m rollups with both p90/p95 and distribution histograms.
5) Alerting: set provisional alerts at warning thresholds to the pilot SRE rotation only (no pager to product until week 4).

Experiment plan and failure injection:
- Day-zero smoke tests: synthetic traces for p99 token latency and token drop rates.
- Week 3 chaos exercise: induce controlled GPU eviction on a single pod to validate fallback model routing.
- Week 5 partial load spike: ramp background traffic by 25% for 30 minutes to verify autoscaling and burst capacity.
- All experiments use dedicated Jira tickets and pre-approved blast radius.

Runbook skeleton (to be completed per route):
- Symptoms -> Quick triage checklist -> Containment steps -> Routing fallback steps -> Post-incident actions + owner assignment.
- Include exact queries to run in observability UI and archived example traces.

Risk register (top items):
- Metric noise: noisy percentiles leading to false positives. Mitigation: smoothing windows, percentiles + histogram checks, and a quiet warning stage.
- Fallback incompatibility: fallback model returns semantically different outputs. Mitigation: semantic sanity checks in shadow responses and auto-fallback thresholds.
- Escalation overload: product teams paged too early. Mitigation: pilot uses human-in-loop for first 4 weeks.
- Unintended data leakage: shadow copy includes PII. Mitigation: redact fields at proxy and use synthetic traffic for sensitive routes.

Communication plan:
- Weekly 30-min sync with pilot stakeholders (Wednesdays).
- Daily 15-min standup for the first 2 weeks of the quiet launch.
- Asymmetric comms: internal channel for SRE/Observability (private), broader status update to GTM/CS once per week with sanitized metrics.
- Pre-approved customer messaging templates stored in linked_artifacts for rapid use.

Measurement & reporting templates (what we'll track):
- SLI time-series (p95 latency, error rate per 1k requests, availability by route).
- Operational metrics (retry rate, queue depth, batching efficiency, kv-cache hit ratio).
- Human metrics (on-call handoff time, runbook execution time, incident learning items).

Rollout decision criteria (go / no-go):
- Go to enforcement: if SLIs show stability across 21 days with MTTR within goal and no high-severity regressions.
- Expand pilot: if SLIs show improvement but operational confidence needs more coverage (add two more routes).
- Rollback: if customer-visible errors spike beyond quiet-path fraction or safe fallback cannot be guaranteed.

Checklist for team docking (per-team):
- Observability queries validated and dashboard created (Y/N)
- Runbook completed and handed to SRE rotation (Y/N)
- Quiet-path routing configured and tested (Y/N)
- Synthetic injection run executed (Y/N)
- CS messaging template reviewed (Y/N)

Open questions to resolve in week 0–1:
- Exact SLA language for quiet-path traffic fraction and how it factors into product SLAs.
- Template for semantic sanity checks on fallback outputs.
- Access policy for archived pilot traces for product vs platform teams.

Appendix: links and quick references
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-IDS/REL-DOCK-87
- Pilot Jira epic: JIRA-REL-1123 (contains experiment tickets)
- Ops repo PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-config/pull/243

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally framed as a low-friction, observable-first pilot. The language and thresholds are provisional — the goal is to produce a repeatable docking template that scales to more teams without surprising customers. Please add comments inline or drop notes in the weekly sync doc thread.
